Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2017. Unemployment is 4.4%, the policy rate is 0.91%, and VIX is about 10.4. The 2-year yield is 1.28% and the 10-year is 2.21%.

The fed funds rate near 0.91% fits mid-2017, after the March and June hikes. Unemployment of 4.4% fits either May 2017 (4.3%) or a later month. The 3-month change in the unemployment rate is -0.4, which is hard to square with 2017, so I checked 2017 values: Jan 4.7, Feb 4.6, Mar 4.4, Apr 4.4, May 4.4 (as first published), Jun 4.3.

Fed funds at 0.91% matches Mar–May 2017 (0.79 in March, 0.91 in April and May, 1.04 in June). The 3-month change of +0.34 fits May, since February was about 0.55. Unemployment was 4.4% in March, 4.4% in April and 4.3% in May at first print, and was later revised to 4.4% in May. The 3-month change of -0.4 against February's 4.7% (as revised then) also fits May, as does the 12m change of -0.6.

Headline CPI at 2.2% YoY fits May 2017 (1.9%) less well than April (2.2%). Core CPI at 1.89% fits April (1.9%). The 10-year yield at 2.21% fits April–May (it was 2.30% in April and 2.21% at end of May), and the 2-year at 1.28% fits May.

US equities returned +1.2% in the month, which fits May (+1.4%). The 3-month return of +1.1% is low, which fits April or May. I'll pick May 2017 with the CPI caveat, since CPI is published mid-month and May's CPI would only be released in June.
